paragraphs: In the morning, align robotic-arm and electrical-control communications. At midday, tune control algorithms with software teams. In the afternoon, commission the line and review cycle times. In the evening, write commissioning reports and periodically sign off on cycle-time and yield targets.

In short, they make mechanical, electrical, and software systems work together. They define systems, develop controls, configure PLC communications, integrate and commission equipment, support operations, and drive automation.
